The most visited museum in Paris is the.why: People name the Louvre as the most visited museum in the world (370 exact hits for that sentence) and say it stands in Paris; a ranking of Paris's own museums is mostly written to place the runners-up, and the Louvre's top place there is an aside. Reading 10 of the 163 hits of "most visited museum in Paris": 4 state the Louvre outright ("The Louvre is also the most visited museum in Paris" and similar), 2 more say "after the Louvre" about the Musée d'Orsay, and 4 rank other museums (the Pompidou second or third, the Orsay third, the Rodin fourth). That is roughly 60 to 100 incidental statements in a corpus where the world-level sentence has 370 and "Louvre in Paris" 65,449; 41 hits are "second most visited museum in Paris" alone, and the exact sentence forms have 20 hits or fewer. It is the kind of fact a travel writer works out for a listing, not one that stands alone the way the Louvre's world rank does, so it is rated derived; it is the borderline one of the two derived edits.
